LESSON: LISTENING AND SPEAKING 7.1.1 PRONUNCIATION AND INTERACTIVE LISTENING

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 7
Topic 7.1: Listening and Speaking 7.1.1 Pronunciation and Interactive Listening
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Listening and Speaking 7.1.1 Pronunciation and Interactive Listening, part of Strand 7 in Grade 6 ENGLISH LANGUAGE.

Key inquiry question: How do you interrupt a speaker politely during a conversation? 2. What emotions or feelings do we show on our faces when talking?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. practise saying the sounds: /ɒ/ as in, of, on, from, lot; hot, /ɔː/ as in door, sort, short, ball, call, or among others,

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Listening and Speaking 7.1.1 Pronunciation and Interactive Listening together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Digital Literacy: The learner’s ability to use digital devices is enhanced while watching partial dialogues on

video, computer, tablets and other devices and responding to questions appropriately.

• Communication and Collaboration: The learner’s ability to speak clearly and effectively is developed as they take

turns during a conversation.

Values:
Peace: This is cultivated as the learner avoids hurting others by practising the skills of turn taking and interrupting

appropriately during conversations.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Life Skills (Self-esteem): The learner’s self-esteem is promoted as they practise effective communication while

engaging in the role-play and retelling the events in the story.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The skill of interactive listening is relevant to the learning of listening skills in Kiswahili.
